SMTO-CTX-0014 — SMTO lost its place while reading an attached file

GUID: fd42d584-c55f-4fd3-ad9b-6f25b831407e
Slug: context-read-invalid-cursor
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • SMTO was reading a file you attached in parts, but its bookmark no longer matched the file, for example because the file was replaced. It stopped instead of reading the wrong version.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going for a step or two. SMTO sees this message and usually starts a fresh read on its own.
  2. If it repeats, tell SMTO in the conversation: "Read the attached file again from the beginning." A fresh read gives SMTO a bookmark that matches the current file.
  3. If you replaced the file with a new version, say which version SMTO should use. SMTO won't mix parts of two versions, so it needs to know which one you mean.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps show text from the attached file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep re-attaching the file to fix this; one fresh read is enough.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A read_context call supplied a cursor that is malformed or whose context ID, content digest, encoding or position does not match the current source revision (invalid_cursor).

What this means

  • Cursor decoding, source identity, content digest or nonnegative position validation failed; a cursor from another revision cannot identify a safe continuation. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Cursor decoding, source identity, content digest or nonnegative position validation failed; a cursor from another revision cannot identify a safe continuation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the selected source and revision with the cursor's origin; malformed cursors and changed content both require a fresh page.

How to fix it

  • Start a new read of the selected source without a cursor and continue with the freshly returned next_cursor; cursors are bound to the source's context_id and sha256 (native/context_reads.py read_source).
  • Start a new read of the selected source and use its freshly returned cursor.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A cursor returned by the current source successfully continues that same revision.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
